title: Competing callable, member and query-block roots were recovered without hiding sibling failures

observed: An unknown callable left invalid argument diagnostics in the envelope.
A dependent outer derived/CTE column diagnostic obscured the inner alias root.
A callable with an invalid owner/member argument retained the dependent member error as a competing root.
firstObservation.compatibilityObservation: The first recovery implementation regressed P_MISC_07_ConvertFunction_SqlServerStyle by suppressing the established MQ3001_UnknownColumn root for CONVERT(varchar, Population).

authority.rule: Schema/source, alias, column/property and callable-owner/name/arity roles retain their precedence; dependent nodes after an invalid root are suppressed while independent sibling roots remain source ordered.

changes: Suppress only argument diagnostics inside an unresolved callable or invalid-arity callable span, while preserving independent diagnostics.
Treat the established SQL Server-shaped CONVERT(type, value) contract as a dialect boundary so its unresolved type token remains the reported MQ3001 root.
Mark CTE values containing a diagnostic recovery root and suppress only dependent consumer diagnostics when the recovered table is referenced by an outer query block.
Retain source-ordered sibling errors for independent columns, aliases and properties.
Keep the recovery helper outside the existing visitor partial budgets and verify the maintainability baselines remain unchanged.
repair.rejectedApproach: Blanket query-wide suppression was rejected because it hides independent sibling roots and makes an expected code appearing somewhere in a cascade look like a correct primary diagnosis.

finalReviewer.evidence: Reviewed the exact 48-case matrix, callable/member/query-block recovery paths, the CONVERT compatibility regression, 66 adjacent tests, 4 maintainability checks and the fresh all-target Release gate.
